newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice up on talk of Iraq buying 75,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice up on talk of Iraq buying 75,000 T.

text.p: Market talk that Iraq has bought 75,000 tonnes of rice coupled with paddy rice hoarding by local traders pushed Thai rice prices up sharply in the week to Thursday, trade soruces said.

They said Iraq bought around 75,000 tonnes of rice, mostly 15 percent grade, for January-March shipment at the price of around $355 per tonne FOB Bangkok. This included around 30,000 tonnes the country bought from recent tender.
Shipping sources said a vessel was loading 20,000 tonnes of rice at the Bangkok port for delivery to Iraq.
"We heard that Exim (Export-Import) bank will help with the credit (to Iraq). So, the market expects more buying from that country,' one trader said.
Benchmark 100 white B grade shot up to $370-400 per tonne FOB Bangkok from $325-355 last week. The 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted around $620-625 on the same basis.
Market sources said some local rice traders hoarded unhusked rice in anticipation that prices would rise higher, reducing the amount of available rice in the market.
"Only a small amount of rice entered the market while there are loads of ships coming to get the rice," said an official from Thai Rice Mills Association.
Many in the market expected the Philippines, one of Thailand's major rice buyers, to announce its import requirement after completing its rice inventory survey earlier on Thursday.

Although the country's rice stock as of January 3 rose 26 percent to 1.739 million tonnes against 1.374 million tonnes a year ago, Thai exporters said they did not think that would substantially reduce the Phillipines' rice importsthis year.
The Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero earlier said he expected the country to import between 300,000-500,000 tonnes of rice in 1997.
